title: Wellwisher / Planner
question: Which Planner composition should we carry forward? All three support work and leisure intentions, drag-and-drop suggestions, protected commitments, open capacity, and optional pinning to an exact time.

options.label: Intentions shelf
options.thesis: Keep unplaced work and leisure ideas visible in a shelf, then arrange them across a spacious weekly horizon. Planning feels like placing possibilities, not filling a calendar.
options.viewport: desktop planner, responsive to stacked shelf and horizon on mobile
options.risk: The week horizon can become too calendar-like if the suggested state is not visually distinct enough.

options.label: Selected-day lanes
options.thesis: Plan one day at a time through three clear lanes: Protected, Suggested windows, and Open capacity. The user gets precision without being forced into exact scheduling.
options.viewport: desktop day planning canvas, stacked lanes on mobile
options.risk: The selected-day focus may make the larger week harder to hold in mind.

options.label: Allocation board
options.thesis: Make the whole week directly rearrangeable: seven day columns, a side summary, unplaced intentions, Rebalance, and Undo. This is the most powerful planner, but needs the strongest guardrails against over-planning.
options.viewport: desktop week planner, horizontally scrollable on mobile
options.risk: The board can become a productivity control surface if every open space feels like a gap to fill.
